intro.title: Build fallback long polling endpoint
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a fallback long polling endpoint using Node.js. You will learn how to create a simple HTTP server that holds client requests open until new data is available, simulating real-time updates. The core programming concept involves managing asynchronous operations and request timeouts with JavaScript's setTimeout and clearTimeout. You'll use Node.js built-in modules like http to handle incoming requests and send delayed responses. This technique provides a reliable fallback for scenarios where more advanced real-time protocols like WebSockets are not supported.
intro.usecase: Long polling endpoints serve as a reliable fallback when WebSocket connections fail in real-time applications. You'll see this pattern in collaborative tools like Google Docs, where document changes must sync across users even with spotty connections. In live dashboards for monitoring systems or financial trading platforms, long polling ensures critical data updates reach users when persistent connections aren't available. Developers implement this as a robust alternative to maintain functionality in diverse network conditions.
